weather conditions through the Grande Ronde Valley. Winds expect

as low as 23 percent.

Warning for wind and low relative humidity, which is in effect
until 7 PM PDT this evening.

Oregon.

are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can

...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 9 AM TO 7 PM CDT SATURDAY DUE TO

GUSTY WINDS, LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY, AND CRITICALLY DRY FUELS FOR
PORTIONS OF NORTH CENTRAL, NORTHWEST LOUISIANA, PORTIONS OF SOUTH
CENTRAL, SOUTHWEST ARKANSAS, NORTHWEST LOUISIANA, SOUTHEAST OKLAHOMA,
EAST, AND NORTHEAST TEXAS...

The National Weather Service in Shreveport LA has issued a Red Flag
Warning in effect from 9 AM to 7 PM CDT Saturday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Portions of north central and northwest Louisiana.

* TIMING...For the first Red Flag Warning, until 1 AM CDT Saturday.
For the second Red Flag Warning, from 9 AM to 7 PM CDT Saturday.

* WINDS...For the first Red Flag Warning, north winds 10 to 20 mph
with gusts up to 35 mph, and for the second Red Flag Warning,
northeast winds 5 to 15 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Minimum Relative Humidity between 25 to 35
percent.

* FUELS...Critically to Extremely Dry.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
Follow all fire restrictions. One less spark, one less wildfire.

A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions that
promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-threatening. This
does not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either occurring
now or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple ways to
receive information from authorities.

Please advise the appropriate officials or fire crews in the field of
this Red Flag Warning.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 16 at 9:32AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
AQAPSR

The Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ) has issued a
PM-10 High Pollution Advisory for Pinal County today.

An episode of strong and gusty winds is forecast to generate
widespread blowing dust that may result in local PM-10 concentrations
that pose a health risk. Adverse health effects increase as air
quality deteriorates.

Coarse particulate matter - also known as PM-10 - is an air
contaminant that can aggravate heart and lung disease conditions,
especially in older adults, children, and those with asthma. A
decrease in physical activity is recommended.

Consolidate your travel, stabilize loose soils, slow down or avoid
travel on dirt roads, reduce or eliminate fireplace use, and avoid
using gas-powered lawn equipment.

For details on this High Pollution Advisory, visit the ADEQ internet
site at www.azdeq.gov/forecast/WestPinal or call 602-771-2300.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 16 at 8:30AM AKDT until October 16 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Rain showers following a strong system continues through Friday
morning, keeping potential for flooding along small creeks. Multiple
waves moving up brought  persistent moderate to heavy rain for much
of the southern half of the panhandle, with the heaviest rain
expected through Thursday night.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The following area, Southern Inner Channels. This includes
the cities of Ketchikan And Metlakatla.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM AKDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.
Street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are possible.
Isolated landslides are possible in areas of steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rain amounts for the Ketchikan and Annette Island area have
reached around 4 to 6 inches, with higher rain totals up to 8
inches falling by the morning along favoring southern facing
mountain sides. While the heavy rain has largely ended this
morning, the multiple rounds of heavy rainfall from Thursday and
overnight keep potential for flooding and ponding over roads into
the morning hours.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

All residents on or near mountain slopes should be prepared for
possible landslides.

properties.headline: Dust Storm Warning issued October 16 at 9:25AM MST until October 16 at 11:30AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Phoenix has issued a

* Dust Storm Warning for...
Pinal County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 1130 AM MST.

* At 925 AM MST, a plume of dust was located over Bapchule, or near
Sun Lakes, and was stationary along Interstate 10.

HAZARD...Less than a quarter mile visibility with strong winds in
excess of 40 mph.

SOURCE...Satellite observations and spotters.

IMPACT...Dangerous life-threatening travel.

* Locations impacted include...
Bapchule, Santan and Sacaton.

This includes AZ Interstate 10 between mile markers 170 and 176.
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not drive into a dust storm. PULL ASIDE STAY ALIVE!

Dust storms lead to dangerous driving conditions with visibility
reduced to near zero. If driving, avoid dust storms if possible. If
caught in one, pull off the road, turn off your lights and keep your
foot off the brake.

There is no safe place on a highway when a dust storm hits.
Visibility can be lost immediately, making it difficult or impossible
to slow down and avoid stopped vehicles. Delay travel, or safely exit
the highway before the dust storm arrives.

CMAMtext: NWS: DUST STORM WARNING til 11:30 AM MST. Be ready for a sudden drop to zero visibility.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: DUST STORM WARNING for this area until 11:30 AM MST. Be ready for sudden drop to zero visibility. Pull Aside, Stay Alive! When visibility drops, pull far off the road and put your vehicle in park. Turn the lights off and keep your foot off the brake. Infants, the elderly and those with respiratory issues urged to take precautions.

Saturday from 11 AM to 7 PM CDT.

behind a cold front today. For Saturday, north winds around 15

properties.instruction:

are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures will
create favorable weather for rapid fire growth and spread. Avoid
activities that promote open flames and sparks.
